Every figure on this page names the population it was measured on. Unless stated otherwise,
that is the held-out {{< var ews.test_share >}} of the booked book: {{< var ews.n_test >}}
accounts the model never saw while it was fitted, {{< var ews.n_events_holdout >}} of them
deteriorating ([7.2](data.qmd#ews-split)). Three things are measured, and they are not the
same: the **model's ranking** (capture, PR-AUC, AUC), the **tiers** cut from it, and the
**triggers** beside it.

## The headline {#ews-headline}

{{< include ../../_generated/ews-headline.md >}}

**Top-decile capture** is the measure the review workflow uses. Rank the held-out accounts by
the model's probability, take the riskiest tenth — {{< var ews.top_k >}} accounts — and count
the deteriorations among them: {{< var ews.capture_events >}} of the
{{< var ews.n_events_holdout >}}, so capture is {{< var ews.capture >}}. A random tenth would
hold a tenth of them; the ratio is the lift, {{< var ews.lift >}}×. Put another way, a
relationship manager working the top decile finds a deterioration in
{{< var ews.top_decile_rate >}} of the accounts called, against {{< var ews.base_rate_holdout >}}
for an account picked at random.

**PR-AUC** (average precision) summarises precision across every cut of the ranking, not just
the top tenth. A ranking with no information scores about the base rate, so the gate asks for
more than that: {{< var ews.pr_auc >}}, {{< var ews.pr_auc_over_base >}} times the base rate
of {{< var ews.base_rate >}}.

**AUC** is reported, not gated. At {{< var ews.auc >}} it would fail any gate set for an
origination model on this platform; why that is the data and not the model, and why the gate
is on capture instead, is the next section and [7.9](gate.qmd).

### How firm each result is

The intervals come from {{< var ews.boot.n >}} bootstrap resamples of the held-out accounts,
drawn with the platform seed, as for D4 and D5 (`wiki/facts/ews_facts.py`):

- **Capture: met, narrowly.** The gate needs {{< var ews.gate.capture_events_needed >}} of the
  {{< var ews.n_events_holdout >}} deteriorations in the top decile; the model has
  {{< var ews.capture_events >}}, a margin of {{< var ews.gate.capture_events_margin >}}
  accounts ({{< var ews.gate.capture_margin_pp >}} percentage points). The interval,
  {{< var ews.boot.capture.lo >}} to {{< var ews.boot.capture.hi >}}, straddles the
  {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}} gate, and {{< var ews.boot.capture_below_gate >}} of the
  resamples fall below it. Another held-out sample of the same size, from the same book, could
  well have failed (finding 3, [7.7](limitations.qmd)).
- **PR-AUC: met, firmly.** The interval, {{< var ews.boot.pr_auc.lo >}} to
  {{< var ews.boot.pr_auc.hi >}}, lies wholly above the base rate;
  {{< var ews.boot.pr_auc_at_or_below_base >}} of resamples fall at or below it. But the gate
  asks only for a ranking better than none ([7.7](limitations.qmd#ews-observations)).
- **AUC: above its sanity floor.** The interval, {{< var ews.boot.auc.lo >}} to
  {{< var ews.boot.auc.hi >}}, lies wholly above the {{< var ews.gate.auc_floor >}} floor.

## The ceiling {#ews-ceiling}

Because the data are generated, the best ranking any model could achieve is known: rank the
accounts by the generator's own deterioration logit without its noise term
(`wiki/facts/ceiling.py`, the only code in this documentation that reads the generator's
truth; it grades the data, not a model). A second reference point is a model, not the truth:
a reference LightGBM, configured as the committed one, given **every observable column** —
{{< var ceiling.ews.oracle_model.n_columns >}} columns: the portfolio's columns outside the
deny-list and the aggregated panel features — fitted on the same training accounts, as the workshop's
`oracle_ceiling.py` does.

{{< include ../../_generated/ews-ceiling.md >}}

**Compare only within a row's sample.** The first row is measured over all
{{< var ews.n_book >}} booked accounts, the rest over the held-out accounts. The figure quoted
in `train.py`'s gate note and in `ews/docs/enhancement_notes.md` as the "oracle ceiling" is
the first row. Setting it beside the model's held-out {{< var ews.auc >}} makes the model look
close to the maximum; they are two different samples. On the held-out accounts themselves the
noise-free logit reaches {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}}, and the model falls short of
it by {{< var ceiling.ews.gap_holdout >}}: it gets {{< var ceiling.ews.share_of_reach >}} of
the way from a coin toss to the ceiling.

**The model is indistinguishable from the reference model.** The reference LightGBM, with
every observable column, reaches {{< var ceiling.ews.oracle_model.auc >}} on the same
accounts: the committed model is a hair below it, well inside the AUC interval above. That is
one learner with one configuration, fitted once; it shows that more columns of the same data
did not help a model like this one, not that no better model exists. Much of the remaining
distance to the noise-free logit plausibly lies in information no observable column holds:
the generator's strongest driver of deterioration is the true PD ([7.2](data.qmd#ews-label)),
and the bank sees only the scorecard's estimate of it. That attribution is a reading of the
generator's code, not a decomposition.

### Why this is the reason the gate is on capture

An AUC gate set where the origination models are gated, {{< var score.gate >}}
([D4.9](../score/gate.qmd)), would be unreachable here: not by this model only, but by any
model, even one ranking by the generator's noise-free logit, which reaches
{{< var ceiling.ews.latent_holdout >}} on these accounts. A gate no honest model can pass invites
one of two failures: a model that is never accepted, or a gate quietly lowered until one is.
Early Warning was instead gated, from its first commit, on what its use needs: does the riskiest
decile, the accounts a review team can actually call, hold well more than its share of the
trouble? Even the noise-free logit captures only {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_capture_holdout >}}
in its top decile on these accounts (PR-AUC {{< var ceiling.ews.latent_pr_auc_holdout >}}), so a
capture gate at the {{< var ews.gate.capture_min >}} level is reachable where the design brief's
was not. The level itself was not derived from the ceiling, and it sits close to what the
committed model achieved — which is why the narrow margin is a finding (finding 3,
[7.9](gate.qmd#history)). AUC stays on the page, reported against the ceiling, so no reader has to take its absence on
trust. That is the honest-gate design ([7.9](gate.qmd)), and it is not a limitation of the
model; how narrowly the committed model clears the gate is (finding 3).

## Benchmark: the score alone {#ews-benchmark}

The simplest early warning a bank could run is to re-rank its book by the origination score.
On the same held-out accounts:

| Ranking | AUC, held-out accounts | Top-decile capture, held-out accounts |
|---|---|---|
| Committed EWS model | {{< var ews.auc >}} | {{< var ews.capture >}} |
| Scorecard PD alone (`pd_score`) | {{< var ews.pd_score.auc >}} | {{< var ews.pd_score.capture >}} |

The model leads on AUC by {{< var ews.pd_score.diff >}}. Because both rankings are scored on
the same accounts, the comparison is a paired bootstrap: {{< var ews.boot.n >}} resamples,
each scoring both on the same resampled rows. The 95% interval for the model's lead is
{{< var ews.pd_score.diff_lo >}} to {{< var ews.pd_score.diff_hi >}}: **it contains zero.**
On AUC the model is not distinguishable from the score it consumes — no measurable gain, and
no measurable loss. On capture, `pd_score` alone falls below the gate where the model clears
it; that is one measurement each, with no paired interval for the difference, and the model's
own capture interval straddles the gate. This chapter does not claim that Early Warning ranks
better than the score alone: finding 4 ([7.7](limitations.qmd)).

## Held out against the whole book {#ews-held-out-vs-whole-book}

The portal scores the whole booked book, and so does every chart drawn from it. Over the whole
book the same model looks far stronger:

{{< include ../../_generated/ews-insample.md >}}

**Only the first row is a performance measure.** The whole book is mostly the model's training
rows — {{< var ews.n_train >}} of {{< var ews.n_book >}} — and on those the model is almost
perfect (training AUC {{< var ews.train.auc >}}, [7.3](methodology.qmd#the-model-lightgbm)).
The whole-book capture of {{< var ews.whole.capture >}} is mostly the model recognising
accounts it has already seen; it says nothing about the next account it will score. The
held-out {{< var ews.capture >}} does. This is the trap Session 3 taught by setting these two
capture figures side by side, and the numbers on its slide are these facts. The portal's own summary endpoint quotes the
held-out metrics recorded at training, which is right; but the tier counts and the watchlist
it serves are computed over the whole book, and they inherit the problem
(below, and findings 1 and 2).

The session video teaches the same point. The tier counts it shows are the whole book's,
{{< var ews.tier.High.n >}} High of {{< var ews.n_book >}} — {{< var ews.tier.High.share >}} by
construction — not what a new account should expect (below).

{{< yt S3-c5 >}}

## Tiers on the held-out accounts {#ews-tiers-held-out}

{{< include ../../_generated/ews-tiers.md >}}

![Observed deterioration rate and mean model probability by risk tier, held-out accounts; the dashed line is the book's base rate.](fig/tier-calibration.svg){#fig-tier-calibration}

**The tiers rank.** The observed deterioration rate falls from
{{< var ews.tier_ho.High.observed >}} in High to {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.observed >}} in
Medium to {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.observed >}} in Low: lifts over the base rate of
{{< var ews.tier_ho.High.lift >}}×, {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.lift >}}× and
{{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.lift >}}×.

**The tiers do not hold their mix.** Built to hold {{< var ews.tier.High.share >}} of the
book, the High tier holds {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.share >}} of the held-out accounts —
{{< var ews.tier_ho.High.n >}} accounts — and catches {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.recall >}} of
their deteriorations. Medium swells to {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.share >}}. A new account,
scored out-of-sample like these, will rarely be High: finding 1 ([7.7](limitations.qmd)).

**Calibration by tier.** For each tier, observed rate over mean probability, against the
tolerance the monitoring plan applies, {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}} to
{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}, counted only on at least
{{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} events — here deteriorations — the same floor rule as
D4 and D5 ([7.8](monitoring.qmd)):

- High: {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.ratio >}} on {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.events >}}
  deteriorations, {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.status >}};
- Medium: {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.ratio >}} on {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.events >}},
  {{< var ews.tier_ho.Medium.status >}};
- Low: observed {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.observed >}} against a mean probability of
  {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.predicted >}}, a ratio of {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.ratio >}} on
  {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.events >}} deteriorations — outside the tolerance and above the
  floor, so a finding (finding 5).

The Low tier is where most accounts sit and where the probability is read least carefully;
it holds {{< var ews.tier_ho.Low.recall >}} of the held-out deteriorations.

## Triggers {#ews-trigger-performance}

{{< include ../../_generated/ews-triggers.md >}}

Book counts and shares are over all {{< var ews.n_book >}} booked accounts: the triggers are
rules, not fitted, so the whole book is a fair population for how often they fire. Precision
— the deterioration rate among flagged accounts — and recall — the share of deteriorations
flagged — are on the held-out accounts, to sit beside the model's figures. **Lift is
precision over the book's base rate** ({{< var ews.base_rate >}}), not over the rate among
unflagged accounts.

What the table shows:

- **No trigger is dead, but one clause is.** Every trigger fires on some accounts. The
  `DELINQUENCY` rule's configured clause, `dpd_max` at or above
  {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.threshold >}}, fires on
  {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.n_alone >}} accounts by itself: `dpd_max` never
  exceeds {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_max.feature_max >}}. The trigger is, in
  effect, `dpd_recent` above {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.clause.dpd_recent.threshold >}}
  (finding 6).
- **The triggers discriminate only modestly.** Their precision runs from
  {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.precision >}} (`DELINQUENCY`) to
  {{< var ews.trigger.high_utilization.precision >}} (`HIGH_UTILIZATION`), against a base rate
  of {{< var ews.base_rate >}}: lifts of {{< var ews.trigger.delinquency.lift >}}× to
  {{< var ews.trigger.high_utilization.lift >}}×, against the High tier's
  {{< var ews.tier_ho.High.lift >}}×.
- **Together they fire on most of the book.** {{< var ews.trigger.any.share >}} of accounts
  ({{< var ews.trigger.any.n >}}) carry at least one trigger, and
  {{< var ews.trigger.multi.share >}} carry two or more. On the held-out accounts, a flagged
  account deteriorates at {{< var ews.trigger.any.precision >}} against
  {{< var ews.trigger.none.rate >}} for an unflagged one; the flags reach
  {{< var ews.trigger.any.recall >}} of deteriorations by flagging most accounts (finding 7).

## Tiers and triggers together {#ews-tiers-and-triggers}

Over the book, as the portal shows them side by side:

| | Accounts | Share |
|---|---|---|
| High tier with at least one trigger | {{< var ews.overlap.high_with_trigger.n >}} | {{< var ews.overlap.high_with_trigger.share >}} of the High tier |
| High tier with no trigger | {{< var ews.overlap.high_no_trigger.n >}} | the rest of the High tier |
| At least one trigger, not High | {{< var ews.overlap.triggered_not_high.n >}} | {{< var ews.overlap.triggered_not_high.share >}} of triggered accounts |
| … of which Low | {{< var ews.overlap.low_with_trigger.n >}} | |

Most High-tier accounts come with a reason a reviewer can raise; some come with only the SHAP
reasons. Among the held-out accounts, the count of High-tier accounts with no trigger is
{{< var ews.overlap.high_no_trigger_ho.n >}}. The two layers are independent by design ([7.3](methodology.qmd)); the High tier
without a trigger is recorded as an observation ([7.7](limitations.qmd#ews-observations)).

## The watchlist {#ews-watchlist}

`watchlist` returns the top {{< var ews.watchlist.top_n_default >}} accounts of the scored
book by probability: the module's default watchlist. The portal serves the top
{{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n >}} of the same ranking by default (`/api/ews/watchlist`), and the
v1 page shows {{< var ews.watchlist.page.n >}}. Over the book as the portal scores it:

| | Value | Population |
|---|---|---|
| Accounts on the list | {{< var ews.watchlist.n >}} | the watchlist |
| … in the High tier | {{< var ews.watchlist.high_n >}} | the watchlist |
| … with no trigger | {{< var ews.watchlist.no_trigger_n >}} | the watchlist |
| … that are the model's training rows | {{< var ews.watchlist.n_train >}} | the watchlist |
| … that are held-out accounts | {{< var ews.watchlist.n_holdout >}} | the watchlist |
| Deterioration rate on the list | {{< var ews.watchlist.rate >}} ({{< var ews.watchlist.events >}} accounts) | the watchlist: **in-sample, not a performance measure** |
| Deterioration rate, held-out members only | {{< var ews.watchlist.holdout_rate >}} ({{< var ews.watchlist.holdout_events >}} of {{< var ews.watchlist.n_holdout >}}) | far too few to measure anything |
| Top {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n >}}, the portal's default: training rows, deterioration rate | {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.n_train >}}; {{< var ews.watchlist.portal.rate >}} | the portal's watchlist: **in-sample** |
| Top {{< var ews.watchlist.page.n >}}, the v1 page: training rows, deterioration rate | {{< var ews.watchlist.page.n_train >}}; {{< var ews.watchlist.page.rate >}} | the v1 page's watchlist: **in-sample** |

The module's watchlist is almost entirely accounts the model was fitted on, and what the portal
and the v1 page show is entirely so; their near-perfect hit rates are the model remembering
those accounts' labels. It is the most visible in-sample number on the
platform and the easiest to misread: finding 2 ([7.7](limitations.qmd)). The honest guide to
what a call list of the riskiest accounts will find is the held-out top decile's rate,
{{< var ews.top_decile_rate >}}.

## Stability

No population stability index is computed for the model's features. The training and
held-out accounts are a random partition of one book, so a PSI between them would measure
sampling noise, not drift; and there is no second period to compare (D4 finding 1,
[7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-the-label-looks-forward)). The one PSI recorded is the tier mix,
held out against the book — {{< var ews.tier_ho.psi_vs_book >}} — which measures the in-sample
problem of finding 1, not drift. The monitoring plan carries stability over time
([7.8](monitoring.qmd)).
